newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to build third pipeline from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to build third pipeline from Iraq.

text.p: Turkey is planning to build another oil pipeline to raise the capacity of the existing twin pipeline from Iraq's Kirkuk oilfields to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, a senior pipeline official said.

"A third pipeline which will run parallel to the existing ones will be built to increase the overall capacity to 120 million tonnes a year," said Mustafa Murathan, general manager of the state pipeline concern Botas.
"But the plan is yet at a preliminary stage," he told reporters late on Wednesday. He did not give other details.

The existing 986-km (613-mile) twin pipeline, which had remained shut until December because of a U.N. trade embargo placed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990, has an annual capacity of 80 million tonnes, or 1.6 million barrels per day.

Iraq, which pumped out about one-third of its oil exports through the line before the embargo, resumed limited oil exports worth $2 billion in December for six months under a U.N.-monitored scheme to buy food and medicine for its people.
